## Overview

Fixes #61912. Retain the KV blocks of preempted requests until their in-flight load reports arrive, so failure handling can invalidate the cache and apply the requested failure policy.

Depends on #61769, whose aborted-owner fix is kept as a prerequisite commit. This adds the preempted-owner handling requested in #61912; running-owner recovery remains in #53298. [Incremental diff above #61769](https://github.com/Lewis-panda/vllm/compare/7238ccdf6d3ae8166bb8d16e8fc14a3f507bdd1f...53aa9dd3965860e455dafd87eda29afd59a23316). I'll rebase after #61769 merges.

## Claims

- Evict the rejected prefix and dependent suffix even after preemption.
- Discard samples from affected outstanding steps; terminate the owner under `fail`.
- Drain retained outputs before readmission, including after a failed prefix-cache reset.

## Validation

At `2dcb854d`, the CPU selection passed **501 tests**; unchanged `7238ccdf` production code with that revision's tests gave **476 passes and 25 intended regression failures**. The current head also passes **501 CPU tests**. Python 3.12, PyTorch 2.13 CPU; mocked connector and worker outputs. Applicable pre-commit checks passed.

The invalid-block suite has 63 cases. The 16 tests added by `2dcb854d` cover public producer-role scheduling pressure, reset followed by `schedule(N+1)`, and a longer prompt reaching the failed load's last block. At that revision, seven failed without the fix; successful-load controls passed.

[Guanxin independently validated the implementation at `89a93299`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/61912#issuecomment-6220454763) on GB200/Qwen3-0.6B, greedy, two trials per cell, standalone and combined with #53298 at `1eca68f4`. Under `fail`, the owner terminates and a subsequent request matches full recomputation; under `recompute`, both requests match that baseline. Successful-load controls are unchanged. Those GPU tests inject preemption directly. Since `89a93299`, changes are limited to tests, comments and diagnostic log wording; recovery logic is unchanged.

<details>
<summary>CPU test command</summary>

```bash
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES="" VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=0 \
VLLM_ENABLE_V1_MULTIPROCESSING=0 .venv/bin/python -m pytest -q \
  tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py \
  tests/v1/core/test_async_scheduler.py \
  tests/v1/core/test_output.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_kv_connector_lifecycle.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_remote_decode_lifecycle.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_remote_prefill_lifecycle.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_scheduler_kv_connector_override.py \
  tests/v1/core/test_prefix_replay.py \
  tests/v1/worker/test_logits_processor_loader.py \
  tests/distributed/aux_output_connector/test_store.py \
  tests/config/test_aux_output_config.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_kv_load_failure_recovery.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_invalid_blocks_correctness.py
```

</details>

## Details

While load N is in flight, pressure or reset can preempt its owner and release its blocks. When report N arrives, scanning running requests misses that owner. Retaining its block IDs before release lets failure handling evict the dependent suffix, discard stale samples and apply `fail` before readmission.

The conservative admission guard can delay requests, including no-load connector requests; latency is unmeasured. Physical block-ID reuse by another request before the report remains the separate #61905 allocation-identity problem. Public-pressure tests use a producer-role mock; they do not establish reachability through a production synchronous-loading producer connector.

Thanks @guanxingithub for the preemption report and GPU validation, and @ArijitDeb for #61769 and the public-scheduler, reset-ordering and longer-prefix probes behind these regressions.

Thanks @Lewis-panda. I ran the CPU selection from the description on `2dcb854d` and on `7238ccdf` with this PR's test file: 501 passed, and 476 passed with 25 failed, matching your numbers. The scheduler code is the same as `89a93299`, which I reviewed in #61912; only tests have been added since.

Of the 16 new tests, the 7 that fail on `7238ccdf` are all failed-load cases: the four producer-role pressure cases, reset-then-`schedule(N+1)` under `recompute`, and both longer-prompt cases. Every load-ok control passes on both trees. Reset-then-`schedule(N+1)` under `fail` also passes on `7238ccdf`, consistent with my probes: the next `schedule()` readmits the owner before the report, and the report then fails it while it is running. With only the admission gate removed (the `gate-ablation.patch` from my follow-up probes), exactly one of the 16 fails: reset-then-`schedule(N+1)` under `recompute`, where the step N+1 token is delivered. So the gate has its own regression test here.

The new tests cover the public-scheduler pressure, reset-ordering, and longer-prefix cases I raised in #61912.

Three small, non-blocking suggestions:
- In `test_reset_then_schedule_discards_rejected_next_frame`, consider also asserting `owner.request_id not in second.num_scheduled_tokens`. That would make the gate's intended readmission behavior explicit alongside the output assertions; the ablation already shows this is a valid regression test.
- The comment in `reset_prefix_cache()` about forcing "preemption + resumption in the same step" could mention that requests with retained in-flight records now wait for those records to drain.
- The new retained-record branch in `_handle_invalid_blocks()` adds preempted owners to `total_failed_requests` without adding their affected tokens to `total_failed_tokens`. Could the "tokens affected" log account for those owners, or make that exclusion explicit?

AI-assisted (Claude, Codex): test runs, code review, cross-checking, and drafting help. The conclusions are mine.

Thanks @ArijitDeb for checking both trees. In [`53aa9dd3`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/commit/53aa9dd3965860e455dafd87eda29afd59a23316), added the explicit readmission assertion and clarified the reset comment. For the log, I used your explicit-exclusion option: both policies now say the token count excludes preempted requests, since their computed-token counters have already been reset.

The CPU selection still passes all 501 tests. Removing only the admission gate makes all four reset cases fail at the new assertion; keeping the old log wording fails both failed-load cases.

Codex-assisted implementation and validation.

+@pytest.fixture
+def pipeline_size():

+@pytest.fixture(params=["fail", "recompute"])
+def sync_load_scheduler(request, pipeline_size):
+    vllm_config = create_vllm_config(kv_load_failure_policy=request.param)
+    vllm_config.scheduler_config.async_scheduling = False
+    vllm_config.parallel_config.pipeline_parallel_size = pipeline_size
+    scheduler = create_scheduler(vllm_config)
+    scheduler.connector = create_mock_connector()
+    scheduler.connector.get_num_new_matched_tokens.side_effect = lambda req, _: (
+        max(0, req.num_prompt_tokens - scheduler.block_size),
+        False,
+    )
+    scheduler.connector.request_finished.return_value = (False, None)
+    scheduler.connector.take_events.return_value = ()
+    return scheduler
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("delay_free", [False, True])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("pipeline_size", [1, 2])
+def test_aborted_sync_load_invalid_suffix_evicted(
+    sync_load_scheduler, delay_free, pipeline_size
+):
+    """An abort must not hide a failed load or its dependent cached suffix."""
+    scheduler = sync_load_scheduler
+    block_size = scheduler.block_size
+    request = create_request(
+        num_tokens=8 * block_size, common_prefix_len=8 * block_size
+    )
+    scheduler.add_request(request)
+    scheduled = scheduler.schedule()
+    (block_ids,) = scheduler.kv_cache_manager.get_block_ids(request.request_id)
+    scheduler.connector.request_finished.return_value = (delay_free, None)
+
+    scheduler.finish_requests(request.request_id, RequestStatus.FINISHED_ABORTED)
+    assert (request.request_id in scheduler.requests) == delay_free
+    assert scheduler.kv_cache_manager.get_block_ids(request.request_id) == (
+        list(block_ids) if delay_free else [],
+    )
+    pool = scheduler.kv_cache_manager.block_pool
+    expected_ref_count = int(delay_free or pipeline_size > 1)
+    assert all(pool.blocks[bid].ref_cnt == expected_ref_count for bid in block_ids)
+
+    scheduler.update_from_output(
+        scheduled,
+        create_model_runner_output([request], invalid_block_ids={block_ids[3]}),
+    )
+    assert all(pool.blocks[bid].block_hash is not None for bid in block_ids[:3])
+    assert all(pool.blocks[bid].block_hash is None for bid in block_ids[3:])
+
+    if delay_free:
+        scheduler.update_from_output(
+            scheduler.schedule(),
+            create_model_runner_output([], finished_sending={request.request_id}),
+        )
+    scheduler.connector.get_num_new_matched_tokens.return_value = (0, False)
+    scheduler.connector.get_num_new_matched_tokens.side_effect = None
+    next_request = create_request(
+        num_tokens=8 * block_size, common_prefix_len=8 * block_size
+    )
+    scheduler.add_request(next_request)
+    next_scheduled = scheduler.schedule()
+    cache_hit_tokens = (
+        next_request.num_computed_tokens
+        - next_scheduled.num_scheduled_tokens[next_request.request_id]
+    )
+    assert cache_hit_tokens == 3 * block_size
+    assert not scheduler._finished_inflight_kv
+
+
+def test_aborted_successful_sync_load_preserves_cache(sync_load_scheduler):
+    scheduler = sync_load_scheduler
+    request = create_request(num_tokens=8 * scheduler.block_size)
+    scheduler.add_request(request)
+    scheduled = scheduler.schedule()
+    (block_ids,) = scheduler.kv_cache_manager.get_block_ids(request.request_id)
+    scheduler.finish_requests(request.request_id, RequestStatus.FINISHED_ABORTED)
+
+    scheduler.update_from_output(
+        scheduled,
+        create_model_runner_output([request]),
+    )
+
+    assert all(
+        scheduler.kv_cache_manager.block_pool.blocks[bid].block_hash is not None
+        for bid in block_ids
+    )
+    assert not scheduler._finished_inflight_kv
+
+
+@pytest.fixture(params=["fail", "recompute"])
+def preempt_load_scheduler(request):
+    config = create_vllm_config(
+        kv_load_failure_policy=request.param, max_num_batched_tokens=256
+    )
+    config.scheduler_config.async_scheduling = True
+    scheduler = create_scheduler(config)
+    scheduler.connector = create_mock_connector()
+    scheduler.connector.request_finished.return_value = (False, None)
+    scheduler.connector.take_events.return_value = ()
+    scheduler.connector.has_pending_block_frees.return_value = False
+    scheduler.connector.has_pending_push_work.return_value = False
+    return scheduler
+
+
+def _start_sync_load(scheduler):
+    block_size = scheduler.block_size
+    request = create_request(
+        num_tokens=8 * block_size, common_prefix_len=8 * block_size
+    )
+    scheduler.connector.get_num_new_matched_tokens.side_effect = (
+        _make_get_num_new_matched_tokens({request.request_id: 7 * block_size}, False)
+    )
+    scheduler.add_request(request)
+    scheduled = scheduler.schedule()
+    (block_ids,) = scheduler.kv_cache_manager.get_block_ids(request.request_id)
+    assert len(block_ids) == 8
+    assert scheduled.num_scheduled_tokens[request.request_id] == block_size
+    assert scheduler.defer_block_free
+    scheduler.connector.get_num_new_matched_tokens.side_effect = None
+    scheduler.connector.get_num_new_matched_tokens.return_value = (0, False)
+    return request, scheduled, list(block_ids)
+
+
+def _preempt_sync_load(scheduler, request, drop_stale_output=False):
+    # Isolate preemption from the memory-pressure fence, which may disallow it.
+    scheduler.running.remove(request)
+    scheduler._preempt_request(request, 0.0, drop_stale_output=drop_stale_output)
+    assert request.status == RequestStatus.PREEMPTED
+
+
+def _finish_preempt_load_test(scheduler):
+    scheduler.finish_requests(list(scheduler.requests), RequestStatus.FINISHED_ABORTED)
+    scheduler.update_from_output(scheduler.schedule(), create_model_runner_output([]))
+    assert_scheduler_empty(scheduler)
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("failed", [False, True])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("async_scheduling", [False, True])
+def test_preempted_sync_load_policy_and_output(
+    preempt_load_scheduler, failed, async_scheduling
+):
+    """Rejected samples must not escape; success retains lossless preemption."""
+    config = preempt_load_scheduler.vllm_config
+    config.scheduler_config.async_scheduling = async_scheduling
+    config.parallel_config.pipeline_parallel_size = 1 if async_scheduling else 2
+    scheduler = create_scheduler(config)
+    scheduler.connector = preempt_load_scheduler.connector
+    request, scheduled, block_ids = _start_sync_load(scheduler)
+    _preempt_sync_load(scheduler, request)
+    result = scheduler.update_from_output(
+        scheduled,
+        create_model_runner_output(
+            [request],
+            invalid_block_ids={block_ids[3]} if failed else None,
+            token_id=999,
+        ),
+    )
+    outputs = [out for group in result.values() for out in group.outputs]
+    assert list(request.output_token_ids) == ([] if failed else [999])
+    assert [token for out in outputs for token in out.new_token_ids] == (
+        [] if failed else [999]
+    )
+    pool = scheduler.kv_cache_manager.block_pool
+    assert [pool.blocks[bid].block_hash is not None for bid in block_ids] == (
+        [True] * 3 + [False] * 5 if failed else [True] * 8
+    )
+    assert not scheduler._finished_inflight_kv
+    if failed and not scheduler.recompute_kv_load_failures:
+        assert request.status == RequestStatus.FINISHED_ERROR
+        assert [out.finish_reason for out in outputs] == [FinishReason.ERROR]
+        assert request.request_id not in scheduler.schedule().num_scheduled_tokens
+    else:
+        resumed = scheduler.schedule()
+        reused = (
+            request.num_computed_tokens
+            - resumed.num_scheduled_tokens[request.request_id]
+        )
+        assert reused == (
+            3 * scheduler.block_size if failed else request.num_prompt_tokens
+        )
+        scheduler.update_from_output(
+            resumed, create_model_runner_output([request], token_id=321)
+        )
+        assert list(request.output_token_ids) == ([321] if failed else [999, 321])
+    _finish_preempt_load_test(scheduler)
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("drop_stale_output", [False, True])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("repeat_failure", [False, True])
+def test_preempted_sync_load_drains_before_readmission(
+    preempt_load_scheduler, drop_stale_output, repeat_failure
+):
+    """No new block generation may hide a pending load; other work can proceed."""
+    scheduler = preempt_load_scheduler
+    request, first, block_ids = _start_sync_load(scheduler)
+    second = scheduler.schedule()
+    assert second.num_scheduled_tokens[request.request_id] == 1
+    _preempt_sync_load(scheduler, request, drop_stale_output)
+    assert not scheduler.schedule().num_scheduled_tokens
+    result = scheduler.update_from_output(
+        first,
+        create_model_runner_output(
+            [request], invalid_block_ids={block_ids[3]}, token_id=999
+        ),
+    )
+    assert [

+        scheduler.connector.get_loaded_kv_cache_group_ids

+    connector.take_events.return_value = ()
+    connector.has_pending_block_frees.return_value = False
+    connector.has_pending_push_work.return_value = False
+    connector.reset_cache.return_value = None

+    requests = {req.request_id: req for req in [*peers, owner]}
+    offers[owner.request_id] = 7 * bs

+    (blocks,) = scheduler.kv_cache_manager.get_block_ids(owner.request_id)

+    result = scheduler.update_from_output(
+        first,
+        create_model_runner_output(
+            [requests[rid] for rid in first.num_scheduled_tokens],
+            invalid_block_ids={blocks[3]} if failed else None,
+            token_id=999,
+        ),

+    owner_outputs = [
+        out
+        for group in result.values()
+        for out in group.outputs
+        if out.request_id == owner.request_id

+    expected = [] if failed or requires_kv_delivery else [999]
+    assert list(owner.output_token_ids) == expected

+    scheduler.update_from_output(

+    else:

+            owner.num_computed_tokens - resumed.num_scheduled_tokens[owner.request_id]
+        )
+        # Pressure reuses the last block even when the load succeeds.
+        assert start == (3 * bs if failed else 7 * bs)
+        scheduler.update_from_output(
+            resumed, create_model_runner_output([owner], token_id=321)
+        )

+    repair = create_request(num_tokens=8 * bs, common_prefix_len=8 * bs, max_tokens=1)
+    for request in [owner, repair]:

+    scheduler.update_from_output(

-            # Clear scheduled request ids cache. Since we are forcing preemption
-            # + resumption in the same step, we must act as if these requests were
-            # not scheduled in the prior step. They will be flushed from the
-            # persistent batch in the model runner.
+            # Clear scheduled request IDs so resumed requests are flushed from
+            # the model runner's persistent batch, even within the same step.
+            # Requests with retained in-flight KV records wait for them to drain.

@@ -3406,6 +3452,25 @@ def _handle_invalid_blocks(
         total_failed_requests += len(sync_failed_req_ids)
         total_failed_tokens += num_failed_tokens
 
+        # Released blocks cannot be repaired in place under either policy.
+        # Scan every record. A request absent from this batch may have
+        # computed its suffix in a later batch using a block that failed here.
+        finished_blocks_to_evict: set[int] = set()
+        for req_id, record in self._finished_inflight_kv.items():
+            for idx, block_id in enumerate(record.block_ids):
+                if block_id in invalid_block_ids:
+                    finished_blocks_to_evict.update(record.block_ids[idx:])
+                    request = self.requests.get(req_id)
+                    if request is not None and not request.is_finished():
+                        # Preemption already reset its counters. Discard all
+                        # outstanding output computed from the rejected KV.
+                        request.drop_stale_output = True
+                        sync_failed_req_ids.add(req_id)
+                        total_failed_requests += 1
+                    break

+            self.kv_cache_manager.evict_blocks(finished_blocks_to_evict)

-                "(failure_policy=fail, %d tokens affected). Request IDs: %s",
+                "(failure_policy=fail, %d tokens affected, excluding preempted "
+                "requests). Request IDs: %s",

                 total_failed_tokens,

@@ -3428,7 +3494,8 @@ def _handle_invalid_blocks(

-            "%d request(s) rescheduled (%d tokens affected).",

Thanks @Lewis-panda. I ran the CPU selection from the description on `2dcb854d` and on `7238ccdf` with this PR's test file: 501 passed, and 476 passed with 25 failed, matching your numbers. The scheduler code is the same as `89a93299`, which I reviewed in #61912; only tests have been added since.

Of the 16 new tests, the 7 that fail on `7238ccdf` are all failed-load cases: the four producer-role pressure cases, reset-then-`schedule(N+1)` under `recompute`, and both longer-prompt cases. Every load-ok control passes on both trees. Reset-then-`schedule(N+1)` under `fail` also passes on `7238ccdf`, consistent with my probes: the next `schedule()` readmits the owner before the report, and the report then fails it while it is running. With only the admission gate removed (the `gate-ablation.patch` from my follow-up probes), exactly one of the 16 fails: reset-then-`schedule(N+1)` under `recompute`, where the step N+1 token is delivered. So the gate has its own regression test here.

The new tests cover the public-scheduler pressure, reset-ordering, and longer-prefix cases I raised in #61912.

Three small, non-blocking suggestions:
- In `test_reset_then_schedule_discards_rejected_next_frame`, consider also asserting `owner.request_id not in second.num_scheduled_tokens`. That would make the gate's intended readmission behavior explicit alongside the output assertions; the ablation already shows this is a valid regression test.
- The comment in `reset_prefix_cache()` about forcing "preemption + resumption in the same step" could mention that requests with retained in-flight records now wait for those records to drain.
- The new retained-record branch in `_handle_invalid_blocks()` adds preempted owners to `total_failed_requests` without adding their affected tokens to `total_failed_tokens`. Could the "tokens affected" log account for those owners, or make that exclusion explicit?

AI-assisted (Claude, Codex): test runs, code review, cross-checking, and drafting help. The conclusions are mine.

Thanks @ArijitDeb for checking both trees. In [`53aa9dd3`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/commit/53aa9dd3965860e455dafd87eda29afd59a23316), added the explicit readmission assertion and clarified the reset comment. For the log, I used your explicit-exclusion option: both policies now say the token count excludes preempted requests, since their computed-token counters have already been reset.

The CPU selection still passes all 501 tests. Removing only the admission gate makes all four reset cases fail at the new assertion; keeping the old log wording fails both failed-load cases.
